title: Dental care when arthritis, frailty and sore hands collide (UK)
meta_title: Dental care when arthritis, frailty and sore hands collide
meta_description: Practical ways to keep teeth, gums and dentures clean when arthritis affects your hands and frailty limits energy, plus dental access and home visits.

direct_answer: Painful hands can make brushing, flossing and cleaning dentures difficult. Electric toothbrushes, chunky handles, interdental brushes with grips and sitting to brush can help. Regular dental check-ups matter, and some areas offer domiciliary dental care for people who cannot get to a dentist.

content:
Looking after your mouth helps you eat, speak and stay comfortable. Arthritis in the hands can make it hard to hold a toothbrush or clean dentures.

This guide covers practical tips and where to get help. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Making brushing easier

  • Try an electric toothbrush, which needs less movement.
  • Make handles thicker with foam tubing or a bicycle grip.
  • Sit down to brush if standing is tiring.
  • Use interdental brushes with long handles.

Dentures

  • Clean over a bowl of water or a folded towel in case you drop them.
  • Use a denture brush with a large handle.
  • Ask your dentist if dentures feel loose.

Medicines and your mouth

Some medicines can cause a dry mouth, which increases tooth decay risk. Sugar-free gum, sips of water and fluoride toothpaste may help. Ask your dentist or pharmacist.

Getting to a dentist

Tell the practice about your needs, such as step-free access or a shorter appointment. Some areas have community dental services or home visits for people who are housebound. Ask your GP, dentist or local NHS service.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can a carer brush my teeth?

Yes. A dental team can show carers how to help.

Is an electric toothbrush better?

Many people with hand arthritis find them easier to use.
